Definition: Reuel, the name of Moses' father-in-law, also of an Edomite and an Israelite
BiblicalUsage: Reuel of Midian is the father-in-law of Moses, the priest whose daughters Moses watered at the well, and whose son Hobab was asked to travel with Israel. The same name also belongs to an Edomite, Esau's son by Basemath, and to an Israelite father in the tribe of Gad.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God weaves one name through many lives, and the father-in-law who sheltered Moses matters as much as any king in the story.
